description: Sequencer that reads its steps off a 64 by 256 grid grown from a one-dimensional cellular automaton, through a movable window that a polyphonic clock splits into rows

params.text: Sets the left edge of the window into the grid, 0 to 64; the window is trimmed if it would run past the right-hand edge
Sets the top edge of the window into the grid, 0 to 256; the window is trimmed if it would run past the bottom
Sets how many cells wide the window is, 0 to 64; at 0 the module stops sending anything
Sets how many cells tall the window is, 0 to 256
Grows the grid again from the cells set on the top bar, using the current RULE and ITER settings, and replaces whatever was there
Chooses which of the 256 elementary automaton rules is used to grow the grid, 0 to 255; the number in use is printed at the right of the display
Puts every channel back to the first cell of its own slice of the window, and releases the four buttons
Sets how many extra passes of 256 rows are run before the grid that is kept, 0 to 1000, each one carrying on from where the last left off
Mirrors the whole grid left to right
Mirrors the whole grid top to bottom

inputs.text: Steps that channel on by one cell on each rising edge, running left to right along a row and then on to the next
Puts every channel back to the first cell of its own slice on a rising edge above 1V
Mirrors the grid left to right on a rising edge above 1V
Mirrors the grid top to bottom on a rising edge above 1V
Shifts the left edge of the window, 6.4 cells per volt, added to the LEFT knob
Shifts the top edge of the window, 25.6 cells per volt, added to the TOP knob
Shifts the width of the window, 6.4 cells per volt, added to the WIDTH knob
Shifts the height of the window, 25.6 cells per volt, added to the HEIGHT knob
Grows the grid again on a rising edge above 1V, as the INIT button does
Shifts the rule number, 25.6 rules per volt, added to the RULE knob and never allowed below 0
Shifts the pass count, 100 passes per volt, added to the ITER knob and never allowed below 0

outputs.text: 5V for one clock pulse when the first channel returns to the start of the window, and nothing at all on the other channels
5V while the clock is high and the cell under that channel is set, so it follows the shape of the clock pulse
5V for as long as that channel stands on a set cell, held until the clock moves it on

notes: The module sends nothing until a clock is patched, and nothing until the grid has been grown: set some cells on the top bar of the display and press INIT.
Clicking a cell on the top bar of the display turns it on or off. The rightmost cell of that bar has a third state, drawn white, which takes the grid down to 63 cells across.
Clicking inside the zoomed view on the right of the display turns that cell of the grid on or off by hand.
A polyphonic clock splits the window into that many equal slices, one per channel, each read from its own starting cell: a 16 by 8 window is 128 steps on one channel and 8 rows of 16 on eight.
The window is drawn as a rectangle on the whole-grid view at the left of the display, with the cells inside it shown large at the right.
menu: Clear Initial State — empties the top bar of the display, so the next INIT grows an empty grid
